plan.name: Observe Python module lifecycles across async calls and threads
plan.summary: Add the gate-owned invariant_observe.module context manager for staged module functions, including identity-preserving registration decorators, async entries and threads started by an entry. It reads copied JSON state through declarative container paths, passes driver arguments only as inputs, counts coroutine resumptions as one call, and accepts a step only after exactly one target call and bounded completion of its owned threads; functional and instance retain their existing restrictions and all forms retain authentication, freshness, poisoning and stateless handles. Module entry defaults may be arbitrary objects used only as inputs and must remain the live function’s own unreplaced defaults; targets keep literal-scalar defaults. Carry module observations through the existing sampled TLC and receipt path, translating lists to sequences without changing raw evidence or granting stronger assurance. Update SPEC.md and README.md with the API, path grammar, timeout, supported forms and refusals, citing D-0183, D-0185 and the other recorded foundations as appropriate; the merger must record the new module observation policy refining D-0183, and run the opt-in Docker suites on the final head when Docker is unavailable to the build.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionModuleObservations
tests.says: Actual Python module read-back binds synchronous and async targets, registration decorators, argument forwarding and step-owned threads, preserving copied ordered JSON state, exact identities, repeatability and replay protection; the same cases run in opt-in Docker.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionModuleEntryDefaults
tests.says: Actual Python accepts synchronous and async module entries with positional and keyword-only Form-call object defaults as inputs, preserves copied state and repeatability, refuses replaced entry defaults before and between steps, and keeps the target literal-scalar rule; the same cases run in opt-in Docker.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationExecutionModuleRefusals
tests.says: A working module lifecycle is admitted, while wrappers, foreign globals, invalid readers or values, unrelated threads, incomplete or multiple calls, timeouts, changed state and caught misuse fail with no accepted observations; functional and instance keep their old restrictions.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationGateModuleObservations
tests.says: Module lists reach sampled Init and Next checking as ordered TLA+ sequences and remain raw JSON in receipts for explicit and omitted components; a bad transition fails while independent tests survive, with real Python by default and real Docker/TLC when opted in.
